summary: ASTRA is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support crew health during long-duration space missions. It brings together physiological indicators, sleep patterns, physical activity, wellness assessments and mission-related health information into a unified dashboard. Using machine learning, ASTRA identifies unusual health patterns and generates explainable alerts, while its AI assistant helps astronauts understand their health trends and access relevant medical information. Designed with offline-first capabilities, the system aims to support continuous health awareness and informed decision-making even when communication with Earth is limited.
details:
ASTRA – Autonomous Spaceflight Health Monitoring & Intelligence System

Problem Statement

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to several health risks, including cardiovascular changes, bone and muscle loss, immune-system alterations, radiation exposure, sleep disruption and psychological stress. Limited medical resources and communication delays make continuous health monitoring and early identification of abnormalities essential.

Our Solution

ASTRA is a web-based health intelligence platform designed to help astronauts monitor, understand and manage their health during space missions.

The platform combines health-data visualisation, machine-learning-based anomaly detection and an AI-powered health assistant to transform health measurements into meaningful insights.

Key Features

  1. Astronaut Health Dashboard: Displays physiological indicators, health trends, sleep patterns and physical activity.
  2. AI/ML Anomaly Detection: Analyses health measurements and identifies unusual patterns relative to individual baselines.
  3. Intelligent Health Assistant: Provides context-aware explanations of health trends and relevant health information.
  4. Emergency Alert System: Generates alerts when monitored readings meet predefined risk criteria.
  5. Mental Wellness Monitoring: Supports periodic assessments of stress, mood, sleep and fatigue.
  6. Mission Control Dashboard: Enables authorised personnel to review crew health information, trends and alerts.
  7. Offline-First Monitoring: Supports local health-data processing and storage when internet connectivity is unavailable, with synchronisation when connectivity returns.

Technology Stack

Frontend: React.js and Tailwind CSS.

Backend: Python and FastAPI.

Database: PostgreSQL.

Machine Learning: Scikit-learn, Pandas and NumPy.

Data Visualisation: Recharts.

Communication: WebSockets.

AI Assistant: Large Language Model with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

Data Sources

The system uses simulated astronaut health readings alongside relevant publicly available NASA research resources and physiological datasets. Simulated data is clearly distinguished from actual research data.

Expected Impact

ASTRA aims to improve astronaut health awareness, support early identification of unusual health patterns, reduce dependence on continuous Earth-based assistance and provide a foundation for intelligent health monitoring during future Moon and Mars missions.

The proposed system is a research and hackathon prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic or treatment system.
